title: fix: add DeepInfra fallback for MiniMax M3
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Fixes upstream rate-limit failures with hidden `minimax/minimax-m3:deepinfra`, using the shared fallback mechanism and exact upstream `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` at `https://api.deepinfra.com/v1/openai`.
- Keeps Fireworks primary, canonical `minimax/minimax-m3`, all four aliases, multiplier 1, Quest access, external hardware, 512K context, vision and tools. Caller prices stay $0.30/$0.06/$1.20 per million input/cached/output tokens; [DeepInfra costs](https://deepinfra.com/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3/api) are $0.28/$0.056/$1.10.
- Passes 146 focused Gen tests, Gen typecheck, Biome and the Enter price snapshot. Direct and forced-fallback E2E verifies native/chat endpoints, aliases, streaming usage, reasoning, tools/raw-message reuse, JSON/schema, 1/2/30 images, prompt/output caches, access and errors.
- Confirms 47 once-billed DeepInfra successes, 47 unbilled primary failures and 28 matching wallet checks. All 10 concurrent short requests pass; three large prompts total 192,880 tokens, above the observed 189,674-token/minute peak.
- Three default-effort coding probes took 106–117 seconds versus 15 seconds on Fireworks. Retains Fireworks as primary; no secret or deployment changes.

gist.headline: A second path for M3
gist.blurb: MiniMax M3 gets a backup route through DeepInfra when Fireworks hits an upstream rate limit. Same model, same caller prices; fewer requests stranded at the gate.
gist.summary: MiniMax M3 keeps Fireworks as its primary provider and gains a hidden DeepInfra fallback using MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 through the shared fallback mechanism, without changing its aliases, capabilities, or caller prices.
gist.impact: Requests that hit a Fireworks rate limit can continue through DeepInfra while retaining MiniMax M3’s 512K context, vision and tools, and $0.30/$0.06/$1.20 per million input/cached/output token prices.
gist.visual_concept: Depict MiniMax M3 as a glowing code-plant fed by two paths: a main Fireworks-labeled terminal and a quieter DeepInfra-labeled backup terminal. Polli, wearing a tiny tool belt, gently tends the backup connection; the two paths show continuity rather than a provider switch.
